overall: Washington, DC is starting the day warm and very humid, with a current temp of 78.8°F at just before 8am and a dewpoint of 71.6°F — well above seasonal norms and supporting a heat index forecast up to 103°F. A broken cloud deck (62% coverage, ceiling ~1,500 ft) is moderating early solar heating, and a Flood Watch is in effect through midnight driven by a slow-moving frontal zone interacting with a deeply tropical air mass. Afternoon convective storms are the dominant uncertainty, expected to arrive around noon and potentially cap the peak before models' projected 14–16h ET maximum.
forecast_obs_notes: The high-resolution dynamical models (GFS 93°F, HRRR 92.2°F, ECMWF 91°F) are tightly clustered well above the NWS official forecast of 90°F, while NBM (85.8°F) skews noticeably lower — likely reflecting the storm-suppression and cloud-feedback effects of the widespread afternoon convection baked into its MOS-style blend. max_temp_prediction: With 78.8°F already observed by 7:49am and a warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr, a simple linear projection to a ~14:00 peak yields roughly 89–91°F, squarely matching the NWS 90°F forecast and the D1_NOW top even bucket (90–91F at 36.5%). The primary downside risk is an earlier-than-forecast storm arrival suppressing the peak into the 86–89°F range; the upside risk is a delayed storm onset allowing the tropical air mass and GFS/HRRR forcing to push temps to 92–93°F. Given the Flood Watch, low cloud ceiling, and 60% PoP by noon, confidence in the 90–91°F bucket is moderate-high for the active even-bucket market.
